items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: I went to a vocal music school when I was four and five run by some people named Jacobs

ctx.x: photograph we had it on I think mm-hmm and there weren't many electrical photographs this was a windup yeah there weren't many so to have a windup one was something in itself I mean to have one photograph in the house was something else in those days oh gosh what about the songs your mother sang to you

she you know I remember particularly her teaching me one of the Eddie Cantor songs from one of his musicals yeah you know potatoes are cheaper and you know it's a time to fall in love yeah I remember I guess somehow I remember the cover of the of the sheet music had a if I remember it right a scantily dressed chorus girl mounted on a on a blazing sky rocket which impressed me at the time but there are also and she also had several old song type collections you know Stephen Foster things when you and I were young…

You still haven't talked about the thing originally entitled the Hiawatha, the Indian and a Mezzo. Do you know what that is? No. That's the original name of the The Lizard on the Rail. Oh really? Yeah, and Tony Perrini recorded it. I thought I would have played that for
